KEY MESSAGE 1...
Surface low pressure begins to exit out to the east this afternoon, 
moving into the New England region. There will be cold air advecting 
in behind the low that will steadily keep temperatures down in the 
mid to upper 40s throughout the day. This will help with some lake 
enhanced rain showers that will mainly impact the western portion of 
the CWA this afternoon as winds will be out of north-northeast. 
Generally expecting around 0.20-0.40" of QPF for areas west of the I-
71 corridor with the highest amounts centered around 
Huron/Lorain/Medina/Richland/Ashland Counties. There will still be 
some residual precipitation across Northeastern Ohio and 
Northwestern Pennsylvania this afternoon into the evening, though 
overall accumulation should be lower than to the west. As 
temperatures begin to drop further after sunset, there could be some 
rain/snow mix across the higher elevations of Northwestern 
Pennsylvania. Not anticipating any accumulation during this time 
period as the ground temperatures will still be above freezing 
given the warm stretch we've had over the past few weeks. Winds 
will begin backing to be more out of the north by late tonight 
early Friday morning creating a lull in the precipitation during
that time. 

KEY MESSAGE 2... 
Late this evening into early Friday morning a shortwave will drop 
down through the Great Lakes rotating around the upper level low 
that will bring reinforcing cold air into the region. 850mb 
temperatures will drop down to around -6C and 500mb temperatures 
down to -25C to -30C by Friday morning. This, on top of the lake 
temperature being in the mid to upper 50s, will support the 
development of lake effect showers across much of the region. Flow 
will shift around to be predominantly out of the north throughout 
the day Friday behind the shortwave. Lingering precipitation will 
continue across Northwestern Pennsylvania Friday morning, and with 
flow at that point still east of north, there will be some 
connection from the northeast that will help fuel those showers. 
There will be some rain/snow mix in that area through the morning, 
especially in the higher elevations of Pennsylvania though most of 
it will be rain. 

As the flow shifts to be out of the north Friday afternoon/evening, 
a lake effect band will begin to develop across the Highlands region 
of Northwestern Ohio. Flow will continue to shift to be more west of 
north by Friday night and the band will shift to cover more of North-
central Ohio for the overnight period into Saturday. Temperatures 
will begin to drop as well with the cooler air moving in with lows 
down into the upper 20s to low 30s. Though, with the marine layer 
staying warmer due to the warm lake, areas near the lake shore 
should stay well above freezing through the period. With that, 
expecting that area to stay with rain with precipitation falls. The 
line from rain to a rain/snow mix will begin around the higher 
elevations of Northern Ohio and Northwestern Pennsylvania, in the 
typical snow belt regions. The axis will continue to shift to the 
east as flow shifts to be northwesterly into Saturday. QPF 
wise, from Friday evening onwards, expecting the highest levels 
to be across the snow belt areas, generally around 0.25-0.50" 
inches. This will be supported by a connection with Lake Huron 
at this point with the shift in the flow. Additionally, with 
temperatures lower Friday night into Saturday, this will 
transition parts of the region to more snow than rain fall. 
Though, with the warmer ground not expecting much accumulation, 
generally less than inch. A few places across Northwestern 
Pennsylvania could see a couple of inches. The majority of the 
area will see a fairly wet, sloppy snow during this event. 

Lake effect showers will continue across Northeastern Ohio and 
Northwestern Pennsylvania Saturday into Sunday. An upper level ridge 
will begin to build into the region late Saturday that will shift 
the flow to be more northwesterly through Saturday night. This will 
create a multiple band set up for that region. Drier air will begin 
to move in as well with the ridge building in that will assist in 
limiting moisture and QPF overall across the area where 
precipitation is continuing. There maybe another burst of moisture 
Sunday during the day as another shortwave moves through the Western 
New York and Pennsylvania region that could bring a quick hit to the 
northeastern parts of the CWA. This will move out by Sunday 
afternoon and precipitation will begin to diminish. Some lingering 
precipitation is possible across Northwest Pennsylvania but little 
to no accumulation is expected. 

Any precipitation is expected to end by early Monday morning as the 
ridge and surface high pressure builds over the region. Dry weather 
is expected afterwards with seasonable temperatures for the 
beginning of the week.
